key_insight: Task-aware fusion of complementary structural encoders and intermediate layers improves materials property prediction over relying on a fixed representation.
engineering_relevance: A lightweight fusion bridge can improve prediction accuracy while reducing trainable parameters and overall training time relative to MatterChat.
method: Use Task-Conditioned Attention Fusion (TCAF) with task-conditioned latent queries.
Combine CHGNet features with intermediate Zatom-1 representations selected for the target property.
Train directly on downstream tasks, jointly learning representation selection and material–language alignment without separate contrastive pretraining.
evidence_signal: Across classification and regression tasks, TCAF outperformed MatterChat with up to 47.8% lower RMSE and half the overall training time; adding UMA-S yielded the highest macro-average classification accuracy of 89.61%.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish generalization to unseen material families or tasks, so validate performance on application-specific held-out data.
paper_title: Choosing the Right Representations: Task-Aware Fusion for Multimodal Materials Language Models
